pr_title: Account for cache type for uploads in AsyncTaskCache
pr_body:
Currently, the AsyncTaskCache for remote execution uses the digest as a key to determine whether or not a task has already been run. Normally this works if there is only a single cache in use. However, when using a disk cache and a remote cache, some calls try to upload files using only a single cache through one code path and another cache through another code path.

This is problematic if only disk caching is used through one code path, when remote caching is enabled though another code path (ie, uploading BES referenced artifacts), the files are not uploaded to the remote cache since the digest is the same. This change uses a String of the digest and the cache type as the key rather than just the digest to allow for uploading to both caches.

The download path is not affected by this bug, so we don't need to make any changes there.

Also, update the combined cache test to reflect what should happen:
when remote_build_event_upload=all, *all* files referenced in the BES
stream are uploaded, including build artifacts (this test now functions as intended based on documentation due to this change).


Fixes #20962, #20296

Maybe I'm thinking about this wrong, but it seems the only way to do this would be to have a base class that by default runs an abstract onFoo method that the disk and grpc classes would override. I'm not sure I see more value in that than just providing a fake.

The real issue with the test is that previously, the test methods would not even be called because they were cached at a higher level and this fake implementation is wrong now. What these series of tests are verifying are that:
 - If thread A and thread B are trying to upload the files, and thread B is canceled, only the futures unique to thread B should be canceled.

I think this is the source of the flakiness, right now, depending on which call happens last, that future gets put into the map and that future is checked. If that future is thread A, then the test passes because it is canceled, but if it is thread B, then it is not canceled.

issue_context.title: When disk cache and remote cache are both enabled, not all test logs are uploaded to the remote cache
issue_context.body:
### Description of the bug:


This should be a pretty generic bug since I've reproduced this on at least 3 different bazel repos on bazel 6.4 and 7.0 and on 3 different remote cache implementations (bazel-remote, buildbuddy, and buildbarn).

Essentially, if you have disk cache enabled with `build --disk_cache=/some/path` and `--remote_cache=grpcs://myserver` not all test logs are uploaded to the remote cache `myserver`. However, if you run bazel test a second time (all tests should be cached, so this is actually a no-op), all the test logs get uploaded then. This assigns a new invocation, however, since the shas of the cached tests are the same, the old invocation's test logs get populated too.

By "not all logs are uploaded", I mean that some logs are uploaded successfully, but others are not even attempted to be uploaded (therefore the bazel timeout and retry options have no effect). I haven't been able to find a correlation between which logs are uploaded and which are not. 

If I remove the `--disk_cache=` arg, all the logs are uploaded on the first try.

### Which category does this issue belong to?


Remote caching

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


`bazel test --disk_cache=~/.cache/bazel --remote_cache=grpc://localhost:9089 --bes_backend=<something> --noremote_upload_local_results --experimental_build_event_upload_max_retries=10 --remote_retries=10 --remote_timeout=1h //...`

I haven't tested without the bes backend, because I use the bes viewer to check whether the logs are there. For bes I used the OSS buildbuddy docker container.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?

Bazelisk version: v1.15.0
Build label: 7.0.1
Build target: @@//src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel:BazelServer
Build time: Thu Jan 18 18:04:46 2024 (1705601086)
Build timestamp: 1705601086
Build timestamp as int: 1705601086

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse master; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text
https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_go.git
54c12e5d6bc591137ca9127a7629a8fc68ab6094
54c12e5d6bc591137ca9127a7629a8fc68ab6094
```


### Is this a regression? If yes, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced.


don't know.

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

No

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

This could be nothing since I'm not very familiar with the bazel source code, but when I instrumented bazel to add logging for this bug, I could see the code path reached here: https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/ByteStreamBuildEventArtifactUploader.java;l=355

but never go to the bytestream grpc uploader here: https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/ByteStreamUploader.java;l=128;drc=aa6fa34f50b4fff74f9085fad76e34681dac3ecb?q=bytestreamgrpc&ss=bazel%2Fbazel

For some reason, [isRemoteFile](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/ByteStreamBuildEventArtifactUploader.java;l=133-136) was returning true for the logs even though they are local files, which I suspect was causing bazel to not upload the logs.

On the second run, the uploads reach the bytestream grpc uploader and are successfully uploaded.
comments: You said that in a fully cached run, the logs always get uploaded. For partially cached runs, is there a correlation between a cache hit/miss and whether the log gets uploaded?
On a cache hit, the logs do get uploaded.

@tjgq I debugged this a little more and basically what seems to be happening is for some reason, RemoteCache calls uploadFile with writePolicy DISK_CACHE_ONLY through some code path (I haven't been able to trace which codepath makes this happen). Then, when the BES upload happens with REMOTE_CACHE_ONLY, since the digest is the key, the AsyncTaskExecutor doesn't execute it because `force` isn't set to true.

Unsure of where the DISK_CACHE_ONLY comes from.

Oddly, `--noremote_upload_local_results` seems to be why we initially try to upload with `DISK_CACHE_ONLY`, however, even if I change that flag to `--remote_upload_local_results`, it still doesn't work (however, it *does* work with my patch above), so maybe I traced the wrong code path...

Thanks for the investigation. This makes the issue look a bit similar to https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/20296. Perhaps the same fix (properly accounting for a combined cache in `AsyncTaskCache`) will work for both cases.

It does sound like the same underlying issue (and the proposed fix is basically what I did in my patch, ironically). Is there a workaround or a plan for a fix for this since it's quite annoying to not have all your assets uploaded to your remote cache (and the linked issue is a few months old)?

Happy to take a stab at a PR myself (hopefully pointing me in the right direction for a fix).

review_comments:
Suggestion: instead of requiring every client to provide two overloads of each method, add default methods for the "no force argument" overload here, so that clients only need to implement the other overload.

(It's also not super clear to me why we need `force = true` at all; the only usage I could find outside of tests is in RemoteRepositoryRemoteExecutor.java, and code history doesn't offer an explanation. But let's not deal with it in this PR - I'll investigate it separately.)
I didn't want to deal with the change of making RemoteCacheClient an abstract class. I feel that can be a follow up change.
